podcast.body: Over the years, Thom Yorke's interest in *Exit Music (For a Film)* waned considerably, which subsequently led to its frequent inclusion in the soundtracks of numerous films and television series. The song has been featured in an estimated five to six films and recently appeared in the soundtrack for *Black Mirror*, establishing itself as a recurring and prominent piece in cinematic contexts. "Today we have it in five, six films, apart from having recently appeared in several soundtracks like Black Mirror and starting to become quite a recurrent song in cinema."

podcast.body: This song predates the recording sessions for *OK Computer* by a year and was not recorded during those sessions, instead being laid down in a standard recording studio. It originated as a commission from the director of the modern *Romeo + Juliet* film (which featured Leonardo DiCaprio) for its end credits. Composed by Thom Yorke, the song is a poetic interpretation of one of the play's most tragic scenes, focusing on Romeo and Juliet's escape to elude death and remain together, a theme distinct from broader narratives of escape from war or general suffering. Thom Yorke was so satisfied with the song's tragic and "pompous" nature that he initially refused its inclusion in the film. The "discography" (likely the record label or producers) also deemed it too tragic and pompous, nearly excluding it from *OK Computer*, but Thom Yorke's persistence ensured its placement midway through the album. Its cinematic theme is a notable departure from the album's focus on modern technology and isolation. "It is a song that already existed before recording OK Computer and was not even recorded during OK Computer."
